results.diagnosis: The add function uses subtraction instead of addition.
The discount_percent parameter needs to be divided by 100 to convert it from a percentage to a decimal multiplier.
The function uses > instead of >= so a score of exactly 60 returns False when it should return True.
The function reverses the entire string character by character instead of reversing the order of words.
The range(n) generates numbers from 0 to n-1, excluding n itself, so sum_up_to(5) returns 10 instead of 15; it should use range(1, n+1) to include all numbers from 1 to n.
Mutable default argument causes the same list object to be reused across function calls, leaking data from previous calls.
The function does not convert words to lowercase before counting, causing different case variations of the same word to be treated as separate words.
The base case only checks if n == 1, but factorial(0) should also return 1; without this check, factorial(0) causes infinite recursion.
The function uses naive substring matching instead of respecting word boundaries, causing partial matches like 'js' to match within 'jsonify'.
The function does not handle division by zero; it should return 0 when the divisor is 0 instead of raising a ZeroDivisionError.
The function does not handle invalid input (non-numeric strings and None values), causing ValueError and TypeError exceptions instead of returning 0.
The function uses an off-by-one error with index len(items) instead of len(items)-1, and doesn't handle the empty list case that should return None.
The function directly accesses dictionary key without checking if it exists, causing a KeyError when the key is missing instead of returning None.
The function uses the union operator (|) instead of the intersection operator (&), returning all elements from both lists instead of only their common elements.
The function converts the string to lowercase but forgets to strip leading and trailing whitespace.
The base case checks if n == 1 instead of n == 0, causing infinite recursion when computing factorial(0) since 0! should equal 1.
The while loop condition uses `low < high` instead of `low <= high`, causing it to exit prematurely without checking the final position where the target might be located.
The function crashes with ZeroDivisionError when given an empty list because it attempts to divide by len(numbers) which is 0.
The function doesn't convert the input text to lowercase before searching for buzzwords, so uppercase or mixed-case buzzwords are not detected.
